chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyih (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khishab, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, and Ali ibn Asbat (as far as I know), from some of their men, who said: Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:

Among the scholars is one who loves to hoard his knowledge and not let it be taken from him; he is in the first degree of Hell. And among the scholars is one who gets insulted when advised and is harsh when giving advice; he is in the second degree of Hell. And among the scholars is one who considers knowledge to be made for the wealthy and noble, and does not consider it to be lowered for the poor; he is in the third degree of Hell. And among the scholars is one who goes in his knowledge the way of the tyrants and rulers; if something is returned to him from his speech or something is shortened in his command, he gets angry; he is in the fourth degree of Hell. And among the scholars is one who seeks the narrations of the Jews and Christians to increase his eloquence and multiply his traditions; he is in the fifth degree of Hell. And among the scholars is one who makes himself available for issuing fatwas and says: Ask me, yet he may not hit upon a single word; and God does not like the pretenders; he is in the sixth degree of Hell. And among the scholars is one who makes his knowledge a means of manliness and intellect; he is in the seventh degree of Hell.
ai.seo_question: What are the seven types of scholars who go to Hell according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith categorizes seven specific archetypes of scholars whose spiritual failure stems from the corruption of their intent rather than a lack of knowledge. It highlights the Shia emphasis on humility, accessibility, and sincerity, warning against the commodification of religious authority and the arrogance that often accompanies scholarly status.
